IEA and WBCSD (2009). Cement Technology Roadmap 2009: Carbon emissions reductions up to 2050. International Energy Agency, Paris, and World Business Council for Sustainable Development, Conches-Geneva. ISBN 978-3-940388-47-6.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 2). The held PDF has 36 pages and lacks the unpaginated centre spread ("Cement roadmap targets", "Regional cement production", "Key regional milestones") listed in the contents, so the regional targets are not available. Successor iea_2018_002 is already extracted; this file adds only what the 2009 edition prints separately: GNR 2006 and 1990 weighted thermal energy of preheater-precalciner kilns (3.382 and 3.605 GJ/t clinker), the GNR range labels (best large kilns 3.0, wet process 6.0 GJ/t; percentiles to other-values), ECRA 2009 post-combustion chemical-absorption capex/opex for a 2 Mt/yr clinker plant (2030: EUR100-300 million and 10-50 EUR/t clinker; 2050: 80-250 and 10-40; incremental to the plant, excluding transport and storage; also derived per t/yr capacity), capture cost EUR20 to over 75/t CO2 captured, IEA MAC USD40-170/t CO2 including transport and storage, 80% reduction efficiency on 6,000 t/d kilns, availability years (capture 2020, oxyfuel 2025). No oxyfuel cost or energy figures and no capture heat/electricity figures are printed (only "+50-120% plant power", in other-values). Electricity per t cement (89/111/130 kWh/t, GNR 2006) is whole-plant and goes to other-values with alternative-fuel shares, emission factors (Annex I), the Annex II baseline and the p.24 roadmap milestone indicators. Not loaded: p.7 projection charts (no printed values), qualitative low-carbon cements (Novacem, Calera, Calix, geopolymer), fluidised-bed kiln (no numbers) and policy text. No price year printed for any cost: 2009 (publication) used. Heating-value basis not stated anywhere. Traps: Annex II header says t CO2/t cement but values are kg; 2006 GJ/t clinker 4.2 in Annex II vs 3.7 global GNR average on p.6; investment-chart labels on p.22 partly garbled in the text layer.
